INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES — MOCK EXAM #10
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
TIME ALLOWED: 90 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 80
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. What is the plural of the English word mango? (1 mark)
   A. mangoss
   B. mangos'
   C. mangoes
   D. mangoies

2. Where should you look to check an answer to a comprehension question? (1 mark)
   A. Back at the text
   B. At the ceiling
   C. In another book only
   D. In your imagination only

3. In Simon says, when should you obey an instruction? (1 mark)
   A. Always
   B. Only when it begins with Simon says
   C. Never
   D. Only if you like it

4. Which way of reading a sad part is best? (1 mark)
   A. Laughing
   B. Slowly and softly
   C. Without pausing
   D. Fast and loud

5. Why is reading fluently important? (1 mark)
   A. It ends the lesson early
   B. It makes the book smaller
   C. It hides mistakes
   D. It helps listeners understand and enjoy the reading

6. What should you keep the same in a paragraph unless there is a reason to change? (1 mark)
   A. The page
   B. The pen
   C. The time of the verbs
   D. The paper colour

7. Which is a part of an oral narrative? (1 mark)
   A. A price tag
   B. The ending
   C. A page number
   D. A stamp

8. What is an oral narrative? (1 mark)
   A. A story kept secret
   B. A written test
   C. A drawing
   D. A story told aloud

9. What does the Kiswahili proverb Haba na haba hujaza kibaba teach? (1 mark)
   A. Only large amounts count
   B. Small amounts added together become a lot
   C. Never save
   D. Big things are useless

10. Which is a proverb? (1 mark)
   A. Bring your book
   B. A stitch in time saves nine
   C. It is Monday
   D. Please sit down

11. Which sentence joins two events with when? (1 mark)
   A. Saw I gift.
   B. I smiled when I saw the gift.
   C. When the gift.
   D. I smiled the gift.

12. What is a personal experience? (1 mark)
   A. A rule
   B. A story from a book
   C. Something that happened to you
   D. A number

13. Where should the comma go in I have money and I want a book? (1 mark)
   A. After want
   B. After I
   C. Before and
   D. After have

14. The bag is below the table. Which preposition fits? (1 mark)
   A. under
   B. on
   C. between
   D. beside

15. Which pair of words rhyme? (1 mark)
   A. cow and shade
   B. hen and goat
   C. day and play
   D. water and food

16. What is a group of lines in a poem called? (1 mark)
   A. A sentence
   B. A paragraph
   C. A stanza
   D. A chapter

17. Which is an interjection? (1 mark)
   A. Hurray!
   B. Table
   C. Beside
   D. Quickly

18. What is leisure time? (1 mark)
   A. Exam time
   B. Sleeping time
   C. Free time when you are not working or in class
   D. Lesson time

19. Which feeling does Ouch! show? (1 mark)
   A. Joy
   B. Pain
   C. Disgust
   D. Sleepiness

20. What is a good way to learn interjections in your mother tongue? (1 mark)
   A. Listen to elders and ask when they are used
   B. Ignore them
   C. Guess meanings
   D. Invent them

21. Which interjection shows a request for silence? (1 mark)
   A. Aha
   B. Shh
   C. Bravo
   D. Hurray

22. Which of these can begin a happy line? (1 mark)
   A. Yuck!
   B. Hurray!
   C. Ouch!
   D. Oh no!

23. Which word in a small silver radio is the noun? (1 mark)
   A. silver
   B. small
   C. radio
   D. a

24. Which adjective describes shape? (1 mark)
   A. loud
   B. heavy
   C. red
   D. round

25. Which question should you ask about an advert? (1 mark)
   A. Who cut it?
   B. How many pages does it have?
   C. What is being sold and how much does it cost?
   D. What is the paper colour?

26. What does the lead of a news item give? (1 mark)
   A. The main facts
   B. The ending
   C. A poem
   D. A joke

27. What is a form? (1 mark)
   A. A page with spaces for information
   B. A picture
   C. A story
   D. A kind of song

28. Which is a polite way to interrupt? (1 mark)
   A. Be quiet!
   B. Stop talking!
   C. Excuse me, may I say something?
   D. You are wrong!

29. What is a stanza? (1 mark)
   A. A rhyme only
   B. A group of lines in a poem
   C. The title
   D. A single word

30. Why do leaders need to give clear instructions? (1 mark)
   A. So people know exactly what to do
   B. To confuse people
   C. To make noise
   D. To waste time

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
31. Describe three rules for writing tidily on lined paper. (3 marks)

32. Write the four parts of a telephone conversation and give a short example of one. (4 marks)

33. Give three uses of capital letters in English. (3 marks)

34. Describe the steps for creating a form for your class about favourite cultural foods. (5 marks)

35. Explain the steps of organising a class debate. (4 marks)

36. Explain how the position game is played with objects on a table. (4 marks)

37. Give three money words and their meanings. (3 marks)

38. List three tips for reciting a poem well. (3 marks)

39. Plan a reader's theatre for a short passage about rain. Say who the roles are, how to practise and how the audience gives feedback. (5 marks)

40. Name two components of a poem. (2 marks)

41. Make an instruction chart of five steps for keeping the class clean. Include a title and start each step with a verb. (5 marks)

42. Explain what an oral narrative is. (2 marks)

43. Explain how you would perform a choral poem with your class. Include voice, pace and non-verbal cues. (5 marks)

44. Name two digital devices and give a use of each. (2 marks)
pages.answers:
INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES — MOCK EXAM #10 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. C — mangoes
   Mango takes es in the plural, mangoes.

2. A — Back at the text
   Good readers go back to the text.

3. B — Only when it begins with Simon says
   The game is about listening carefully.

4. B — Slowly and softly
   A slow, soft voice matches sadness.

5. D — It helps listeners understand and enjoy the reading
   Fluent reading helps meaning.

6. C — The time of the verbs
   Keep past, present or future consistent.

7. B — The ending
   Stories have openings, characters, events and endings.

8. D — A story told aloud
   Oral narratives are spoken stories.

9. B — Small amounts added together become a lot
   The proverb means little by little fills the measure.

10. B — A stitch in time saves nine
   It is a short saying that gives advice.

11. B — I smiled when I saw the gift.
   It uses when to link two events.

12. C — Something that happened to you
   A personal experience is an event you lived.

13. C — Before and
   A comma comes before the joining word.

14. A — under
   Under means below something.

15. C — day and play
   Day and play end in the same sound.

16. C — A stanza
   A stanza is a group of lines.

17. A — Hurray!
   Hurray shows joy.

18. C — Free time when you are not working or in class
   Leisure is free time.

19. B — Pain
   People say ouch when hurt.

20. A — Listen to elders and ask when they are used
   Learning from speakers is reliable.

21. B — Shh
   Shh asks for quiet.

22. B — Hurray!
   Hurray shows happiness.

23. C — radio
   Radio names the thing.

24. D — round
   Round describes shape.

25. C — What is being sold and how much does it cost?
   Buyers check product and price.

26. A — The main facts
   The lead gives the key facts.

27. A — A page with spaces for information
   Forms collect information.

28. C — Excuse me, may I say something?
   It asks permission politely.

29. B — A group of lines in a poem
   A stanza is a group of lines.

30. A — So people know exactly what to do
   Clear instructions get work done safely.

SECTION B
----
31. (3 marks)
   Answer: Letters sit on the base line, tall letters reach the top line, keep a finger space between words, and start on the left.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each rule, up to three.

32. (4 marks)
   Answer: Greet; say who you are and why you called; talk and listen; say goodbye. Example: Good afternoon, this is Neema speaking.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each part and one mark for an example, with 4 marks maximum.

33. (3 marks)
   Answer: The first word of a sentence, names of people and places, the word I, days and months (any three).
   Working / marking points: One mark for each use.

34. (5 marks)
   Answer: Decide the purpose, write a title, list questions such as name, class and favourite food, leave space for answers, write short instructions, test it with a friend and improve it.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each step up to five.

35. (4 marks)
   Answer: Choose a motion, form two teams, plan reasons, take turns to speak for about a minute each, listeners note points, the class votes.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each of four steps.

36. (4 marks)
   Answer: One pupil gives an instruction such as put the pencil on the book. Another follows it. The class checks whether the position is correct. Then the roles are swapped.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each of four points.

37. (3 marks)
   Answer: Trade: buying and selling. Profit: money gained. Customer: person who buys. Price: cost of something.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each word with its meaning.

38. (3 marks)
   Answer: Learn it well, mark pauses and stressed words, speak clearly, look at the audience, keep a steady pace.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each tip.

39. (5 marks)
   Answer: Roles such as narrator, farmer, child and rain. Read your part silently three times, mark stressed words, then read aloud with expression. The audience gives one good point and one improvement.
   Working / marking points: Two marks for suitable roles, two marks for practice steps and one mark for feedback.

40. (2 marks)
   Answer: Title, lines, stanzas, rhyme, rhythm, message (any two).
   Working / marking points: One mark each.

41. (5 marks)
   Answer: Title: How to keep our class clean. 1. Sweep the floor. 2. Wipe the desks. 3. Put waste in the bin. 4. Wash your hands. 5. Close the windows.
   Working / marking points: One mark for the title, one mark for each of four steps that begin with verbs and are in order.

42. (2 marks)
   Answer: An oral narrative is a story told aloud, passed on from person to person, that entertains and teaches.
   Working / marking points: One mark for told aloud and one mark for entertain or teach.

43. (5 marks)
   Answer: Learn the poem well, keep the same pace together, speak clearly with expression, use gestures and smiles as non-verbal cues, look at the audience and practise beforehand.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each of five points.

44. (2 marks)
   Answer: Phone for calling, radio for hearing news, camera for taking photos (any two with uses).
   Working / marking points: One mark for each device with its use.
